headlines.summary: Investors were digesting megacap tech earnings and the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates steady.
headlines.article_text: Stock market today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on July 01, 2026 in New York City. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images U.S. stocks rallied Thursday, rebounding from the prior day's sell-off when the Federal Reserve decided to hold rates steady. Microsoft and semiconductors helped drive the gains. The Nasdaq Composite finished 2.8% higher at 25,122.18, ending a six-day losing streak. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 613.92 points, or 1.2%, to end the day at 52,208.06, while the S&P 500 climbed 1.7% to settle at 7,437.63. Microsoft shares jumped 16%, after reporting growth from its Azure business. Semiconductors rallied, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) higher by more than 8%. Micron Technology surged 18%, while Advanced Micro Devices were up more than 13%. The momentum trade returned, with the iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF (MTUM) higher by more than 5%. Memory stocks surged, and South Korea's memory maker SK Hynix jumped more than 17%. In contrast, Meta Platforms was down 8% after issuing a soft revenue forecast and a 91% drop in second-quarter free cash flow. Nasdaq Composite, 1-day "This is ultimately a tale of two AI investment strategies," said Stephen Evans, chief investment officer at Pave Finance. "One company is increasing profits while spending heavily, while the other is allowing those costs to eat into its bottom line." Stocks recovered following a dismal session. On Wednesday, the Dow plunged more than 1,100 points , marking its worst decline going back to April 2025. A selloff that started earlier in the day accelerated in the late afternoon. Yields spiked, as investors worried that the Fed was falling behind on its fight against inflation. The 30-year yield hovered near 2007 highs. It jumped 6 basis points after regular trading Wednesday to above 5.2%. The rest of the yield curve was little changed. One of the busiest weeks of corporate earnings continues Thursday, with Amazon , Apple and Coinbase set to report after the close. 4 Min Ago Stocks close lower Thursday Stocks closed lower Thursday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 613.92 points, or 1.2%, to end the day at 52,208.06, while the S&P 500 climbed 1.7% to settle at 7,437.64. The Nasdaq Composite finished 2.8% higher at 25,122.18. — Sarah Min 50 Min Ago Hedge funds have likely finished deleveraging from chips, JPMorgan says A worker produces semiconductors at a production line of a semiconductor manufacturer in Binzhou, China, on Jan. 20, 2025. Costfoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images In a good sign for the semiconductor trade, hedge funds and other big investors have likely finished selling their positions in tech, chip and memory stocks in order to reduce their debt levels, JPMorgan analysts said Wednesday. Chip stocks have been selling off like mad in the last few weeks, though multiple investors have characterized it as a temporary – although brutal – speedbump on a longer upward trajectory. The PHLX Semiconductor index was up more than 7% as of 2:45PM ET on Thursday. JPMorgan said the deleveraging has happened more quickly than they expected. "We find that investors deleveraging in the tech and semiconductor space, including memory stocks, has advanced faster than we had previously anticipated," Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou at JPMorgan wrote in a Wednesday note to clients. "As a result, we now see more limited room for any further deleveraging. "We find evidence that the previous increase in leverage by equity focused hedge funds during April/May has been largely unwound," he added. – Tobias Burns 2 Hours Ago UBS initiates a Buy rating for SK Hynix ADR, with a price target of $204 Chey Tae-won, chairman of SK Group, center, Kwak Noh-jung, president and chief executive officer of SK Hynix Inc., center left, and Koh Seung-beom, chairman of SK Hynix Inc., center right, during the company's initial public offering (IPO) at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, US, on Friday, July 10, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images UBS has initiated coverage of SK Hynix with a Buy rating and a $204 price target, implying 61% upside from Wednesday's close of $126.79. "At current valuation, we do not believe SK Hynix shares fully reflect structurally higher memory profitability," wrote UBS analyst Nicolas Gaudois. Gaudois believes the memory semis industry has changed drastically, with accelerating memory demand from agentic AI. UBS expects DRAM demand growth to reach 36% in 2027 from 22% in 2026. SK Hynix is also securing long-term agreements, advancing HBM negotiations for 2027 and expanding capacity, all of which could support stronger margins and long-term growth. — Deena Zaidi 3 Hours Ago Information technology stocks head for best day in over a year Information technology stocks are on track to record their biggest one-day climb since mid 2025. The S&P 500 sector added nearly 5% in Thursday's session, making it the best performing of the 11 that comprise the broad index. If that holds, Thursday would mark the sector's largest daily advance since April 2025. The sector was aided by gains in chip stocks in the session, as well as from Microsoft's post-earnings surge. Thursday's rally pulled the information technology sector into the green on the week. The sector is now up more than 16% in 2026. — Alex Harring 3 Hours Ago Jersey Mike's debuts at $21 per share Jersey Mike's Subs Inc. sandwiches are distributed during the company's initial public offering (IPO) ceremony on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Thursday, July 30, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images Sandwich restaurant chain Jersey Mike's began trading at the New York Stock Exchange on Thursday, with initial trading 9% below its IPO price of $23 per share . The stock opened at $21, though rebounded to around $22.10 minutes into trading. That represents a 3.5% decline from its IPO price. Jersey Mike's sold 43.5 million shares, raising about $1 billion and valuing the company at $7.3 billion. — Davis Giangiulio and Amelia Lucas 4 Hours Ago Stocks making the biggest moves midday A person walks past the entrance to a Crocs store on Feb. 12, 2026, in Miami, Florida. Joe Raedle | Getty Images Check out the companies making the biggest moves in midday trading: Crocs — The shoemaker tumbled more than 10% despite beating fiscal second-quarter expectations and raising its fiscal year forecast. The company's second-quarter margins were weaker than expected, and estimates for the third quarter were also light. Year to date, Crocs stock has gained more than 16%. Microsoft — The tech giant jumped 15% after reporting quarterly revenue of $90.01 billion, topping estimates of $87.62 billion, per LSEG. Azure growth of 43% at constant currency beat StreetAccount estimates of 40.2% growth. The company also said Azure revenue in the 2026 fiscal year surpassed $100 billion for the first time. Meta Platforms — Shares tumbled more than 9% after the company posted earnings per share of $6.18 for the latest quarter, missing analysts' estimates by $1.04 per share, according to LSEG. It also forecasted third-quarter revenue between $61 billion and $64 billion, the lower end of which is lighter than the $63.15 billion estimated by analysts. headlines.article_text: Reddit (RDDT) Q2 2026 earnings report Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Reddit's sales for the second quarter jumped 61% from a year earlier, sailing past estimates. The company also reported earnings that trounced expectations. Reddit CEO Steven Huffman said the company is reckoning with "choppy" search referral traffic. In this article RDDT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Reddit CEO Steve Huffman stands on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) after ringing a bell on the floor setting the share price at $47 in its initial public offering (IPO) on March 21, 2024 in New York City. Spencer Platt | Getty Images Reddit reported second-quarter earnings on Thursday that beat on the top and the bottom lines, and the company issued guidance that sailed past expectations. Here's how the company did compared with LSEG estimates: Earnings per share: $1.25 vs. 95 cents expected Revenue: $805 million vs. $730 million expected Sales for the second quarter rose 61% year-over-year from $500 million a year earlier, the company said in a statement. Net income climbed to $253 million, or $1.25 a share, from $89 million, or 45 cents per share, the previous year . Third-quarter revenue should come in between $860 million to $870 million, the company said, while analysts were expecting $828 million. Reddit said adjusted earnings this quarter will be between $385 million and $395 million, topping Wall Street projections of $368 million. Reddit's revenue rose more than 60% for an eighth straight quarter as the company's ad business continues to benefit from overseas expansion, a rush of new users and continued improvements to its online ad engine. The results come a day after digital ad giant Meta reported a 28% increase in year-over-year revenue. That topped estimates, but the stock sank due to a weaker-than-expected forecast and dwindling cash flow tied to artificial intelligence investments. watch now VIDEO 3:48 03:48 Meta's stock pullback is justified, says Needham's Laura Martin The Exchange watch now VIDEO 3:48 03:48 Meta's stock pullback is justified, says Needham's Laura Martin The Exchange Meta's cash is going the other direction, as the companies investments stay in check. Free cash flow more than doubled to $261 million from $111 million a year ago. The company's global daily active unique users, or DAUq, jumped 18% year-over-year to 130.3 million for the quarter, ahead of analyst estimates of 129.9 million. Its U.S.-specific DAUq rose 6% to 53.2 million. Average revenue per user, or ARPU, came in at $6.18 while U.S. ARPU was $11.85. Reddit's "Other revenue" category, which includes its data licensing business , grew 24% year-over-year to $43 million. The company's two biggest data licensing partners are OpenAI and Google . While Reddit's user base has been expanding, investors have expressed concern about the company's ability to monetize traffic, as Google search referrals come down. CEO Steve Huffman wrote in an investor letter on Thursday that, "Search referrals were choppy in the quarter, and traffic was more volatile later in the quarter." "But the bigger picture is unchanged," he wrote. "The commercial business is strong, our revenue growth is differentiated, and we have much to be encouraged by on the product side." Earlier this month, Reddit shares tumbled after the Wall Street Journal reported that the company was considering cutting off Google's access to its data. Reddit and publishers like USA Today and Politico are concerned that they're receiving less referral traffic as the search giant increasingly pushes its Gemini-powered AI chat service, the report said. A Reddit spokesperson told CNBC at the time that it is approaching negotiations "just like any business should, by focusing on doing what's best for Reddit." Huffman said the company is considering its options. "In AI overviews, we have still yet to find that win-win, but we're still you know collaborative and looking for that," he said. "I don't think there's any simple binary decision here." Michael Yanow | Nurphoto | Getty Images Rivian Automotive reduced its 2026 spending plans and slightly narrowed its previously forecasted losses this year as the company reported second-quarter results Thursday. The revised guidance now include adjusted losses between $1.8 billion and $2 billion, down from $1.8 billion to $2.1 billion, and capital expenditures of $1.7 billion to $1.8 billion, down from $1.95 billion and $2.05 billion. It reconfirmed a previously raised delivery target of 65,000 to 70,000 vehicles to customers. Rivian previously said the raised delivery guidance was driven by higher deliveries during the second quarter of its electric delivery van and flagship R1 products. The company also started delivering its midsize R2 SUV during the quarter. It's ramping up production of that vehicle at its sole production plant in Normal, Illinois, which has capacity to produce 160,000 of the vehicles annually. Rivian said the $250 million reduction in capital spending at the mid-point was enabled by "project efficiencies and timing of spend," which the automaker previously increased to allow for added investments in new technologies such as its hands-free driving system. Rivian's second-quarter revenue included $1.14 billion from automotive and $515 million from software and services. The results were slightly higher than its pre-released second-quarter revenue expectations of between $1.55 billion and $1.65 billion that were released last month in conjunction with disclosing a public offering of 75 million shares of its Class A common stock. Rivian's net loss attributable to common stockholders during the second quarter was $837 million, or 63 cents a share, a $278 million, or 34 cent per share, improvement compared with the second quarter of 2025. headlines.article_text: Apple (AAPL) Q3 2026 earnings report: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu watch now VIDEO 3:24 03:24 Here's how to play this tech giant's stock as it reaches a record high Options Action Apple reports fiscal third-quarter results after the bell. Here's what analysts are expecting, according to LSEG. Earnings per share : $1.89 Revenue : $108.65 billion It's Tim Cook's final earnings call as Apple CEO before he turns over the reins to John Ternus on Sept 1. The report comes as Apple's stock is trading near a record, up 24% so far this year as of Wednesday's close, topping its megacap peers. Revenue is expected to increase 16% from $94 billion a year earlier, according to LSEG. Apple is reckoning with a global memory crunch, or what Cook recently called a " hundred-year flood ," and a rush for chip manufacturing capacity that's already forced the company to lift prices on Macs and iPads. Apple hasn't said it will raise prices on iPhones, but many analysts are expecting hikes as soon as this year. Meanwhile, Apple is gearing up for a launch of a redesigned Siri using Google technology alongside new iPhone hardware in September, a critical test for the company as investors worry that it's fallen behind in artificial intelligence. Still, if the company meets expectations, it will mark a third straight quarter with year-over-year revenue growth of at least 15%. Ternus, a 25-year Apple veteran and Apple's current head of hardware, said little on the prior earnings call, which was held shortly after the CEO transition was announced in April. Investors are eager to hear more. The conference call is scheduled for 5 p.m. ET. Apple stock chart for Thursday, July 30, 2026 CNBC's reporters are covering Apple earnings from bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. 10 Min Ago Down day for Apple's stock watch now VIDEO 1:33 01:33 Apple to report quarterly results in Tim Cook's final earnings call: Here's what to know Power Lunch Apple shares traded lower heading into the third-quarter print. The stock was fell 1.4% for the day to close at $333.43. It's the second straight day of slippage after the stock hit a record on Tuesday, when the company briefly crossed the $5 trillion market cap milestone for the first time. Even with the drop, Apple shares are up about 23% for the year. — Ari Levy 53 Min Ago Trying to keep the streak going Photo taken on Aug. 14, 2023 shows iPhones at an Apple store in Hangzhou, East China's Zhejiang province. On the same day, data released by TechInsights showed that Apple's iPhone sales in China surpassed the United States for the first time in the second quarter of 2023, becoming the largest single market for iPhone shipments. Costfoto | Nurphoto | Getty Images Apple has topped revenue and earnings estimates for 13 straight quarters, dating back to the period ended December 2022. When the company last missed expectations , overall sales for the holiday quarter dropped 5%, the first year-over-year decline since 2019. Cook said at the time that three factors hurt the results: a strong dollar, production issues in China affecting the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the overall macroeconomic environment. "On the third factor, I would say was just the challenging macroeconomic environment, and you're hearing that from, I would think, everybody," Cook said in an interview. — Ari Levy 1 Hour Ago What will Apple say about China? Apple CEO Tim Cook and singer Li Yuchun attend a special event marking Apple's 50th anniversary at the Apple Taikoo Li Chengdu store on March 18, 2026 in Chengdu, Sichuan Province of China. VCG | Getty Images So far this year, Apple has been doing well in greater China, which includes mainland China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Sales in the first half of the year grew in the region by 33%, and Cook said on the last earnings call that he was "thrilled" with the performance. Apple is winning in China as the memory shortage has jacked up device prices across the board, leading the overall market to atrophy. In the second quarter, smartphone shipments declined 4.3%, the fifth straight quarterly drop, according to IDC. Apple has yet to raise iPhone prices in China, allowing it to take market share. the company gained four percentage points "of market share in China year-over-year (18% of total China market shipments in 2Q26) where competitors Samsung, Xiaomi, Vivo, and Oppo have raised prices this year," analysts at Goldman wrote this week. Analysts polled by FactSet are expecting 22% growth in China sales during the quarter to $18.77 billion, —Kif Leswing 3 Hours Ago Apple's gross margin in focus, after nearing 50% watch now VIDEO 1:51 01:51 Apple shares slide as Mac and iPad hikes raise fears of higher iPhone prices Squawk on the Street Apple's gross margin will come into focus on Thursday as investors look to see how the company is grappling with rising costs for memory and other parts for its devices, a dynamic that Cook called "unsustainable" in June. Apple's Android rivals are already seeing their margins suffer . Prices on Macs and iPads went up at the end of June, just before the quarter ended, so the impact of the those hikes won't be seen until the company's September quarter results. Apple's margin has expanded in recent years, hitting a peak of 49.3% in the March quarter. But the company's gross margin on its devices was only 38.7%, which was down 200 basis points, or 2 percentage points, from the previous quarter. And Apple forecast that gross margin in the June quarter would decline, to between 47.5% and 48.5%. Analysts polled by StreetAccount are expecting exactly 48%. — Kif Leswing 3 Hours Ago Apple and Amazon wrap up megacap earnings Amazon CEO Andy Jassy walks to lunch during the Allen & Co. Media and Technology Conference in Sun Valley, Idaho, on July 9, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Along with Apple, Amazon is scheduled to report after the bell on Thursday, bringing an end to earnings season for the megacap tech companies, as Nvidia's report comes later. It's been a mixed bag so far as investors scrutinize capex commentary and start holding companies more accountable for converting expenses to revenue. Meta and Microsoft traded in opposite directions on Thursday, with investors still skeptical of Mark Zuckerberg's spending plans, while Microsoft gets applauded for its cloud growth. Amazon's cloud business will be of particular interest to Wall Street, following results from rivals Alphabet and Microsoft. — Ari Levy 3 Hours Ago Growth expected to slow from here, retreating to more normal levels Looking ahead to the rest of this year and into 2027, growth rates are projected to slow significantly. Consensus expectations for revenue expansion in the fiscal fourth quarter at are about 12%, and that number drops into the single digits for most of next year, according to FactSet. For investors, those types of numbers look familiar. Prior to the December quarter, Apple hadn't notched double-digit revenue growth since 2021. Apple typically issues revenue guidance on its earnings call. — Ari Levy 4 Hours Ago Cook and Ternus make a public appearance John Ternus, Apple's Senior Vice President of Hardware Engineering, (L) and Tim Cook, CEO of Apple, attend the world premiere celebrating season four of the Apple TV beloved series “Ted Lasso” at Academy Museum of Motion Pictures on July 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California.
